moves.name: LS Scan
moves.description: Scans the battlefield. Always hits. Reveals enemy info.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy scans your filesystem with a rapid directory sweep!
challenge.playerPrompt: List all files in the current directory
challenge.tutorialText: ls lists files and directories. Use ls -la to see hidden files (starting with .) and detailed permissions.
challenge.realWorldExample: ls -la ~/Documents shows all files including hidden ones in your Documents folder

moves.name: Cat Read
moves.description: Reads the enemy's secrets. Reliable single-target damage.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy reads your config file and learns your secrets!
challenge.playerPrompt: Display the contents of a file called 'config.txt'
challenge.tutorialText: cat prints file contents to your terminal. Add -n to see line numbers. Used constantly for reading logs and config files.
challenge.realWorldExample: cat /etc/hosts shows your system's hostname-to-IP mappings

moves.name: Echo Shout
moves.description: Shouts a command into the void. Echoes through the filesystem.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy broadcasts a message to all terminals!
challenge.playerPrompt: Print the message 'Hello World' to the terminal
challenge.tutorialText: echo prints text to the terminal. Used in scripts to show messages, create files with >, and debug variable values.
challenge.realWorldExample: echo $HOME shows the path of your home directory

moves.name: Mkdir Build
moves.description: Builds a defensive structure. Medium power, no frills.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy constructs a new directory fortress!
challenge.playerPrompt: Create a new directory called 'projects'
challenge.tutorialText: mkdir creates new directories. Use mkdir -p to create nested directories at once (mkdir -p a/b/c).
challenge.realWorldExample: mkdir -p ~/code/myproject/src creates the full path even if parent dirs don't exist

moves.name: MV Slide
moves.description: Moves the attack sideways — hard to dodge, hard power.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy slides a file across the filesystem!
challenge.playerPrompt: Move (or rename) a file from 'old.txt' to 'new.txt'
challenge.tutorialText: mv moves OR renames files. mv file.txt backup/ moves it to a folder. mv old.txt new.txt renames it.
challenge.realWorldExample: mv report_draft.txt report_final.txt renames your draft to final

moves.name: CP Copy
moves.description: Duplicates the attack force. Hits twice — once for each copy.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy duplicates your data with a swift copy!
challenge.playerPrompt: Copy a file called 'data.txt' to 'backup.txt'
challenge.tutorialText: cp copies files. Use cp -r to copy entire directories recursively. Always copy before editing important files.
challenge.realWorldExample: cp -r myproject/ myproject_backup/ creates a full backup of your project folder

moves.name: RM Erase
moves.description: Deletes the enemy data block. Permanent and devastating.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy erases critical files from your system!
challenge.playerPrompt: Remove a file called 'temp.txt'
challenge.tutorialText: rm permanently deletes files (no recycle bin!). Use rm -r for directories. NEVER run rm -rf / (deletes everything).
challenge.realWorldExample: rm -r build/ cleans up your compiled output folder before a fresh build

moves.name: Grep Hunt
moves.description: Hunts for vulnerabilities in the enemy. High power, slightly unreliable.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy hunts through your logs for your secrets!
challenge.playerPrompt: Search for the word 'error' inside a file called 'app.log'
challenge.tutorialText: grep searches for patterns inside files. -i ignores case, -n shows line numbers, -r searches entire directories.
challenge.realWorldExample: grep -r 'TODO' src/ finds every TODO comment in your source code

moves.name: Find Seek
moves.description: Seeks deep into the system. High power but takes concentration.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy searches the entire filesystem for your hidden files!
challenge.playerPrompt: Find all files named 'readme.md' starting from the current directory
challenge.tutorialText: find locates files by name, type, size, or date. Searches recursively. Extremely powerful for finding things fast.
challenge.realWorldExample: find . -name '*.log' -mtime +7 finds all log files older than 7 days

moves.name: PS Spy
moves.description: Spies on enemy processes. Always hits. Reveals info.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy spies on all running processes in your system!
challenge.playerPrompt: List all currently running processes
challenge.tutorialText: ps shows running processes. ps aux shows ALL processes with CPU/memory usage. Combine with grep to find specific programs.
challenge.realWorldExample: ps aux | grep node finds any running Node.js processes on your machine

moves.name: Kill Shot
moves.description: Sends SIGKILL to the target process. Devastating but hard to land.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy terminates one of your essential processes!
challenge.playerPrompt: Kill the process with PID 1234
challenge.tutorialText: kill sends signals to processes. kill PID is a polite stop request. kill -9 PID is a force kill. Use ps to find the PID first.
challenge.realWorldExample: kill -9 $(lsof -t -i:3000) force-kills whatever is running on port 3000

moves.name: BG Hide
moves.description: Hides in the background. Raises Defense by one stage.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy sends a process to hide in the background!
challenge.playerPrompt: Resume a stopped job and run it in the background
challenge.tutorialText: bg resumes a paused job in the background. Use Ctrl+Z to pause a running program, then bg to resume it backgrounded. fg brings it back.
challenge.realWorldExample: Run a long task, Ctrl+Z to pause it, bg to resume it while you do other work

moves.name: Pipe Combo
moves.description: Chains two commands together. Massive chained damage.
moves.hint: Type: anything | anything (e.g. ls | grep txt)

challenge.enemyText: The enemy chains commands together in a devastating pipeline!
challenge.playerPrompt: List all files and pipe the output to grep to find ones named 'log'
challenge.tutorialText: The pipe | sends the output of one command as input to another. This is one of bash's most powerful features for combining tools.
challenge.realWorldExample: ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep shows only Python processes, excluding the grep itself

moves.name: Ping Probe
moves.description: Probes the enemy with network packets. Reliable mid-range move.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy probes your network with diagnostic packets!
challenge.playerPrompt: Check if google.com is reachable on the network
challenge.tutorialText: ping tests network connectivity by sending packets to a host. Use -c to limit the number of packets. Great for debugging network issues.
challenge.realWorldExample: ping -c 3 8.8.8.8 checks if Google's DNS server is reachable (good basic connectivity test)

moves.name: Curl Pull
moves.description: Pulls data from the enemy server. Solid NETWORK attack.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy pulls data from a remote server at high speed!
challenge.playerPrompt: Fetch the content of https://example.com
challenge.tutorialText: curl makes HTTP requests from the terminal. -s is silent mode, -L follows redirects, -o saves to file. Used constantly for APIs and downloads.
challenge.realWorldExample: curl -s https://api.github.com/users/octocat shows a GitHub user's profile as JSON

moves.name: Wget Fetch
moves.description: Downloads the enemy's HP directly. Relentless fetching attack.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy downloads an entire website to their server!
challenge.playerPrompt: Download a file from https://example.com/file.zip
challenge.tutorialText: wget downloads files from the internet. Unlike curl, it saves to disk by default. Use -r to mirror entire websites.
challenge.realWorldExample: wget https://nodejs.org/dist/v20.0.0/node-v20.0.0.tar.gz downloads the Node.js source

moves.name: SSH Connect
moves.description: Opens an encrypted tunnel through the enemy's defenses.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy opens an encrypted tunnel to a remote server!
challenge.playerPrompt: Connect to a remote server at user@192.168.1.100
challenge.tutorialText: ssh opens a secure encrypted shell on a remote machine. Uses port 22 by default. Use SSH keys instead of passwords for security.
challenge.realWorldExample: ssh deploy@myserver.com connects you to your production server's terminal

moves.name: Chmod Lock
moves.description: Locks down the enemy's permissions. Crushing SYSTEM-type blow.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy locks down file permissions to block your access!
challenge.playerPrompt: Make a script called 'run.sh' executable
challenge.tutorialText: chmod changes file permissions. chmod +x makes a file executable. 755 = owner can do everything, others can read/execute. 644 = standard file.
challenge.realWorldExample: chmod +x deploy.sh lets you run your deployment script with ./deploy.sh

moves.name: Sudo Power
moves.description: Unleashes root-level destruction. The strongest move in the terminal.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy invokes root-level system privileges!
challenge.playerPrompt: Run the command 'apt update' with administrator privileges
challenge.tutorialText: sudo runs commands as the superuser (root). Required for installing software, editing system files, and managing services. Use with caution.
challenge.realWorldExample: sudo systemctl restart nginx restarts your web server with admin privileges

moves.name: Export Boost
moves.description: Exports a power variable. Raises Attack by one stage.

challenge.enemyText: The enemy injects a variable into the global environment!
challenge.playerPrompt: Set an environment variable called PATH_PREFIX to '/usr/local/bin'
challenge.tutorialText: export sets environment variables that are available to the current shell AND child processes. Variables without export are only in the current shell.
challenge.realWorldExample: export NODE_ENV=production tells your Node.js app to run in production mode
